slides.title: Rethinking the Implications of Human Feedback for Preference Learning in Human-Robot Collaboration
slides.tldr: IMPROVING ROBOT PREFERENCE LEARNING VIA DYNAMIC IMPLICATION MODELING
slides.highlight: The proposed IMPLIED method improves how robots infer human preferences from feedback, enhancing behavior adaptation during collaboration. This is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied learning.

card.one_liner: IMPLIED improves robot preference learning by dynamically revising labels for unchosen actions based on feedback.
card.key_idea: A mixture model combining a fixed-rule prior with a Gaussian Process classifier that learns to infer and revise accepted/rejected labels for unchosen actions over time.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via simulation (sandwich-making, block-sorting) and a physical pizza-making study against fixed-rule and LLM baselines using L2 error and conflict proportion.

slides.title: CARLAverse: A Highly Modular, Distributed, and Multimodal Framework for Human-in-the-Loop Simulation
slides.highlight: CARLAverse provides a multimodal simulation ecosystem for human-in-the-loop interactions, supporting the study of social negotiations between humans and agents relevant to HyECHO's focus on hybrid human-AI team states.

card.one_liner: CARLAverse is an open-source, distributed simulation framework for multi-agent human-in-the-loop mixed-traffic research.
card.key_idea: It decouples physics by computing latency-critical ego-dynamics locally on client nodes while a central server orchestrates global traffic and NPC physics.
card.evaluation: Not clearly stated; the paper documents architecture and integration, noting that quantitative validation is addressed in companion publications.
card.limitation: Requires high-performance simulation computers at each local node for rendering and local physics calculations.

slides.title: Exploring Avatar-Based Representations of Desktop Analytical Workflows for Asymmetric Collaborative Visual Analytics
slides.highlight: This research explores avatar-based representations to improve collaborator awareness in asymmetric desktop-VR settings, contributing to the study of embodied interaction relevant to RwB.

card.one_liner: Desk2Avatar represents desktop analytical workflows in VR using avatars to improve collaborator awareness and guidance.
card.key_idea: Translates desktop interactions into two VR avatar modes: 'Distanced' (fixed position, uses orientation/pointing) and 'Embodied' (moves to targets, uses direct touch-based gestures).
card.evaluation: Within-subject study (18 participants) using VAST 2007 dataset; compared avatars against a depth-adaptive cursor via recall accuracy, NASA-TLX, and co-presence scales.
card.limitation: Embodied avatars caused occlusion, distraction, and higher frustration/physical demand, especially during complex analytical tasks.
